Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates a peripheral, oblong opacity in the left mid-to-lower lung zone that forms obtuse angles with the chest wall, a classic radiographic sign of a pleural-based lesion such as a chronic loculated empyema. This morphology distinguishes it from intrapulmonary masses (which typically form acute angles) and diffuse processes like mesothelioma or pneumonia.
